Description: Appreciation for demonstrations directly tied to class deliverables. Apply when the student praises the immediate, applied usefulness of demonstrated AI use for graded coursework (e.g., the truss project, homework, exams).
Do NOT apply when: The student is requesting MORE course-tied content rather than praising content that was delivered (-> DF11). The praise concerns AI capabilities or prompting in general, untied to a course task (-> DF02).
Distinguish from: DF11 (praise of delivered content vs. suggestion for future content); DF02 (course-task utility vs. general capability)
Example responses: "I liked how it showed how it was applied to the truss project." • "it was helpful to know how to utilize AI for the truss project" • "the AI demonstrations where sometimes geared towards our project so it related to work we were doing"

Description: Positive feedback regarding learning novel AI capabilities, prompting techniques, or new platforms (e.g., Gemini). Apply when the student expresses appreciation for discovering what AI can do or how to control it better, independent of a specific graded task.
Do NOT apply when: The appreciation is tied to a specific graded deliverable (-> DF01). The appreciation concerns real-world/industry framing rather than tool capability (-> DF03).
Example responses: "I love how I was introduced to the capabilities of the Gemini, and now it has become my go-to tool for Graph-related questions" • "I liked learning about tips and such that I didn't know before about AI, such as changing the voice/way the AI responds"

Description: Enjoyment derived from seeing AI placed in larger real-world engineering, research, or industry context. Apply when the student praises the broader educational, societal, or research framing rather than immediate class tasks or tool mechanics.
Do NOT apply when: The praise is about tool capability or prompting technique (-> DF02) or applicability to coursework (-> DF01).
Example responses: "I liked the comparison to research studies - places everything in the wider context of academia" • "I liked that they included real world examples, eg when companies like Boeing where mentioned" • "I liked learning about whats going on in the world with AI that I dont learn from other classes"

Description: Valid, constructive positive feedback that does not fit DF01-DF03 and lacks sufficient frequency to form its own category. Describe the like in the notes field.
Do NOT apply when: Any of DF01-DF03 fits, even at low confidence (apply that code and flag instead).
Example responses: "I liked seeing that educators are working on researching / integrating AI use into classes" • "I liked that the AI demonstrations were giving us the ability to use AI instead of pushing the idea that using AI is inherently evil"

Description: Frustration that the baseline AI literacy of the class was underestimated. Apply when the student expresses that they (or students generally) already knew the material presented.
Do NOT apply when: The complaint is that content, however novel, did not help with coursework (-> DF06). The complaint is about density or pacing (-> DF07/DF08).
Distinguish from: DF06 (already known vs. not useful); DF08
Example responses: "Most stuff wasnt new to me" • "I feel like most students knew of the stuff shown in the AI demonstrations" • "They showed things I am willing to bet most college students already know how to do" • "Some felt repetitive or obvious at times."

Description: Frustration that the demos did not assist with immediate course hurdles (homework, core mechanics), including the feeling that demo time displaced core instruction.
Do NOT apply when: The complaint is that material was already known (-> DF05). The student proposes a change to increase applicability without complaining about what was delivered (-> DF11). When both a complaint and a proposal are present, apply both DF06 and DF11.
Example responses: "I struggled to find them applicable to our coursework. They seemed more general and slightly disjointed." • "Sometimes not relevant to the course material and background info" • "not very helpful in terms of homework or any type of solving problem in a traditional way" • "I would have preferred to spend the "AI" sections of the class doing more examples/getting taught more"

Description: Complaints about WHEN and HOW LONG: timing, placement in the lecture, duration, or scheduling of the demonstrations.
Do NOT apply when: The complaint concerns the AMOUNT or COMPLEXITY of content rather than its timing/duration/placement (-> DF08). If a response contains both (e.g., too much content in too little time), apply both DF07 and DF08. The student proposes a logistics change (-> DF13; apply both if a complaint is also stated).
Distinguish from: DF08 (schedule/duration vs. content density); DF13 (complaint vs. suggestion)
Example responses: "It being at the end of class make it difficult to pay attention" • "I disliked how long they were"

Description: Frustration that the demonstrations were too complex, too dense, or induced mental fatigue: too much information to absorb, or content requiring background (e.g., programming) that students lacked.
Do NOT apply when: The complaint is purely about timing, placement, or duration (-> DF07).
Distinguish from: DF07; DF05 (too much new content vs. nothing new)
Example responses: "I felt they were a little bit of an information dump into a small amount of time and so I was confused by the end" • "A Lot of info in a small amount of time." • "some tools, like the virtual sandbox, required a decent amount of knowledge of programming"

Description: Observations that the format failed to hold student attention: boredom, passive distraction, phone usage among peers, or self-reported disengagement.
Do NOT apply when: The student proposes engagement-boosting changes without describing disengagement (-> DF12/DF14); apply both when both are present.
Example responses: "Majority of the time it seemed like students did not really pay attention and rather just went on their phones" • "Honestly it was just not very interesting to most students" • "There were times when I felt like I was not very engaged in some of them"

Description: Valid, constructive negative feedback that does not fit DF05-DF09 and lacks sufficient frequency to form its own category. Describe the dislike in the notes field.
Do NOT apply when: Any of DF05-DF09 fits, even at low confidence (apply that code and flag instead). In particular, complaints reducible to time not well spent for coursework (-> DF06) or to content already known (-> DF05).
Example responses: "Goal was unclear" • "it felt like I was just watching my professor play around with an AI engine"

Description: Recommendations to pivot demonstrations toward immediate academic help: exam preparation, generating practice problems, Socratic tutoring, project assistance, checking homework, or error-finding in student work.
Do NOT apply when: The student only praises course-tied content already delivered (-> DF01) or only complains about lack of utility without proposing a direction (-> DF06).
Example responses: "AI demonstrations should show more ways in how AI can help students study for exams... generating practice problems and solution as well as flash[cards]" • "More things applicable to the class instead of broad view" • "the best way of helping us learn is by seeking how to look for mistakes"

Description: Requests to move away from passive observation: guided, hands-on, class-wide prompting activities where students use the tools themselves, or more interactive formats generally.
Do NOT apply when: The suggestion concerns content applicability (-> DF11) or scheduling/format of delivery (-> DF13).
Distinguish from: DF11; DF13; DF09 (fix vs. observed problem)
Example responses: "Having students join in the demonstration could be helpful, maybe the entire class follows a guide" • "I wish the demonstrations were a bit more interactive beyond just talking to our neighbors" • "More interactive models maybe?"

Description: Suggestions to change how and when the demonstrations are delivered: moving demos to the start of class, making them shorter, or shifting them to optional asynchronous modules (e.g., Blackboard/Piazza video).
Do NOT apply when: The student only complains about logistics without proposing a change (-> DF07). "Make them shorter" is DF13; "they were too long" is DF07; apply both when both are stated.
Distinguish from: DF07; DF12 (format change vs. interactivity change)
Example responses: "maybe making a video and posting it on blackboard or piazza so people can come back to them or if they miss class" • "Start the class with the demos when everyone's focus is high" • "Make them more concise." • "demonstrations at the start of the class would make mores sense"

Description: A valid, constructive suggestion that does not fit DF11-DF13 and lacks sufficient frequency to form its own category. Describe the suggestion in the notes field.
Do NOT apply when: Any of DF11-DF13 fits, even at low confidence (apply that code and flag instead).
Example responses: "I think if there was an incentive people would engage more" • "gauge what the students want to take away from AI first, then conduct the demos" • "show how to use it on different llms"

Description: Student states they did not attend the demonstrations, attended too few to comment, or otherwise cannot evaluate them. Standalone when it is the whole response; if the student also comments substantively on demos they did see, code those comments and add DF15 only if partial attendance is explicitly the reason for limited feedback.
Do NOT apply when: The student attended and simply has no opinion (-> DF16). The response is blank or off-topic (-> DF17).
Distinguish from: DF16 (cannot evaluate vs. evaluated as unremarkable); DF17
Example responses: "I missed most of the demos so I can't really say" (constructed example)

Description: Student attended and reports no strong reaction in either direction, without substantive likes, dislikes, or suggestions. Standalone: if a specific like/dislike/suggestion is also given, code that instead.
Do NOT apply when: Any substantive like, dislike, or suggestion is present. The student could not evaluate due to non-attendance (-> DF15).
Distinguish from: DF15; DF17 (an on-topic neutral evaluation vs. no codable content)
Example responses: "i didnt feel very strongly about them either way"

Description: Responses that are blank, nonsensical, or fail to address the prompt about the demonstrations in any capacity. Standalone.
Do NOT apply when: Any other code can be applied, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead).
